solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flower finally dies now, getting very little rain

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word dies

parts.note: a drop is the smallest amount of rain

explanation.surface: A gardener laments a plant dying off for want of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The early white spring bulb is a common example of a flower.

clue.text: Account local person presented about beheaded wife of Henry VIII

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the local person wraps the other piece

parts.note: a native is someone born in a place

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth and last wife of Henry VIII

explanation.surface: A local tells a story about one of Henry VIII's wives losing her head.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII really did behead two wives, Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard, which tempts you towards them; the one meant is his last wife, who outlived him and was never executed.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a story or narration of events, a synonym.

clue.text: Unrestrained European writer

parts.note: unrestrained means wild, out of control

explanation.surface: A free-spirited European author.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was an Irish playwright and novelist, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Ski slope, perhaps, makes you weak and tired

definitions.meaning: a ski run going downhill, read as two words

explanation.surface: Skiing all day leaves you worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run heads downhill, and someone feeling run-down is fatigued and below par.

clue.text: Source of timber to make aircraft

explanation.surface: Wood is used to build an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane tree is grown for timber, and a plane is also an aeroplane.

clue.text: Droop, faced with a story of epic proportions

explanation.surface: Someone flags when confronted with a very long tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic narrative, originally an Icelandic epic.

clue.text: Terrible traumas in Indonesian island

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of traumas are in a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: Disasters strike an island in Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is one of the large islands making up Indonesia.

clue.text: Gossips principally like to talk a lot

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of the word Gossips

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

explanation.surface: Gossips, above all, love chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is informal for chattering at length.

clue.text: Exam some scholar once rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run of letters is read backwards
some means only part of the words scholar once is taken

explanation.surface: A former scholar turned down a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination.

clue.text: Marines clashing with squadron leader — almost a catastrophe

indicators.note: clashing suggests the letters of Marines are in conflict and jumbled
leader points to the opening letter of squadron

explanation.surface: Marines clash with an air squadron's commander, narrowly avoiding disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a narrow escape from an accident.

clue.text: NB: what a money thief might do

definitions.meaning: nota bene, Latin for mark well

definitions.text: what a money thief might do

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: NB tells a reader to pay attention, and a thief might pocket a banknote.

clue.text: Time to copy recording

explanation.surface: It is time to duplicate a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio or video recordings were long made on magnetic tape.

clue.text: I will have diamonds gift-wrapped for head of state

indicators.note: wrapped means the present encloses the other letters

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone is to receive gift-wrapped diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the elected leader of a republic.

clue.text: Cheap tinsel is out of place in this sacred building

indicators.note: out of place means the letters of Cheap tinsel is are moved about

explanation.surface: Tawdry decorations would look wrong in a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel is the papal chapel in the Vatican, famous for Michelangelo's ceiling.

clue.text: Criticised intricately-woven threads

indicators.note: intricately-woven suggests the letters of threads are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Elaborately woven yarn gets a poor review.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is informal for harshly criticised or panned.

clue.text: Competition cheat put on trial

indicators.note: put on means one piece sits on top of the other in this down entry

explanation.surface: A fraudster in a competition is brought to trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition between rivals.

clue.text: Viewed from the back, a precious stone is great

indicators.note: seen from behind means the words are read in reverse order

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jewel looks splendid even from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for terrific or huge.

clue.text: Like religious person stoic man converted

indicators.note: converted means the letters of stoic man are changed into another form

explanation.surface: A stoic man has undergone religious conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic describes the way of life of a monk, a religious person.

clue.text: Crop of the month, do you say?

indicators.note: do you say signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: the month of May gives May's, belonging to that month

explanation.surface: Someone asks which crop belongs to this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The month' is May, so 'of the month' is MAY'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, also called corn, is a cereal crop.

clue.text: Lots of people in Cornwall region acquiring weapon

indicators.note: acquiring means gaining an addition, so the weapon is attached after the region

parts.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England, abbreviated SW

explanation.surface: Crowds in the west of England take up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a dense crowd of people or insects.

clue.text: Like some tall buildings much liked by fat cats?

definitions.meaning: fat cats are overpaid executives, who love a big pay increase

explanation.surface: Wealthy executives are fond of skyscrapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block is a multi-storey building, and a large pay increase pleases rich bosses.

clue.text: Climber, one going over sides of valley

indicators.note: going over means placed above in this down entry

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sides of means the outer letters of the word valley

explanation.surface: A climber crosses the edges of a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a plant that climbs walls and trees.

clue.text: Tract having articles about religious education

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the subject

parts.note: A and A, two indefinite articles
RE is the British school subject religious education

explanation.surface: A religious pamphlet contains articles about religious education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' suggests a pamphlet but means a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract of land is a region or expanse.

clue.text: Surveyed? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the word Surveyed is removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a scene was looked over and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so'; here it drops half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey is to look at, so looked at is a synonym.

clue.text: Guess I'm conveyed in spacious car

indicators.note: conveyed in means carried inside the car

parts.note: an estate is a large car with a big boot, a station wagon

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they are being driven in a roomy car.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation, a guess.
